current_example.title: Example: Writing a Vector in a Different Basis Given a Linear Relationship Between Two Bases

q-112406.name: Question 1
q-112406.problem: Let $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where ${b}_{1}={c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=-{c}_{1}?$
q-112406.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2} \\  & =2{c}_{2}-{c}_{1} \\  & =2{c}_{2}+(-{c}_{1}) \\  & =2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

q-112406.html:
Question 1
?

Let C={c1,c2} be a basis of R2 and [x]C=[−12]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis B={b1,b2}, where b1=c2 and b2=−c1?

a
[x]B=[2−2]
b
[x]B=[−2−1]
c
[x]B=[1−2]
d
[x]B=[12]
e
[x]B=[21]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]C=[−12], we can write x as follows:

x=−c1+2c2=2c2−c1=2c2+(−c1)=2b1+b2

Therefore, [x]B=[21].

q-112639.name: Question 2
q-112639.problem: Let $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where ${b}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=2{c}_{1}?$
q-112639.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={c}_{1}+3{c}_{2} \\  & =3{c}_{2}+{c}_{1} \\  & =3\cdot 3(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2})+\frac{1}{2}(2{c}_{1}) \\  & =9{b}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].$

q-112639.html:
Question 2
?

Let C={c1,c2} be a basis of R2 and [x]C=[13]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis B={b1,b2}, where b1=13c2 and b2=2c1?

a
[x]B=[912]
b
[x]B=[32].
c
[x]B=[123].
d
[x]B=[192].
e
[x]B=[29].
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since [x]C=[13], we can write x as follows:

x=c1+3c2=3c2+c1=3⋅3(13c2)+12(2c1)=9b1+12b2

Therefore, [x]B=[912].
q-112639.knowledge_point: Writing a Two-Dimensional Vector in a Different Basis

q-34634.name: Question 3
q-34634.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}={b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-5{b}_{1}?$
q-34634.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2} \\  & =-3{b}_{2}+2{b}_{1} \\  & =-3{b}_{2}-2(-{b}_{1}) \\  & =-3{b}_{2}-\frac{2}{5}(-5{b}_{1}) \\  & =-3{c}_{1}-\frac{2}{5}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}].$

q-34634.html:
Question 3
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[2−3]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=b2 and c2=−5b1?

a
[x]C=[−3−2]
b
[x]C=[−352]
c
[x]C=[25]
d
[x]C=[−35]
e
[x]C=[−3−25]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[2−3], we can write x as follows:

x=2b1−3b2=−3b2+2b1=−3b2−2(−b1)=−3b2−25(−5b1)=−3c1−25c2

Therefore, [x]C=[−3−25].
q-34634.knowledge_point: Writing a Two-Dimensional Vector in a Different Basis

q-35260.name: Question 4
q-35260.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=5{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-3{b}_{1}?$
q-35260.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={b}_{1}-5{b}_{2} \\  & =-5{b}_{2}+{b}_{1} \\  & =-(5{b}_{2})-(-{b}_{1}) \\  & =-(5{b}_{2})-\frac{1}{3}(-3{b}_{1}) \\  & =-{c}_{1}-\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

q-35260.html:
Question 4
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[1−5]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=5b2 and c2=−3b1?

a
[x]C=[15−13]
b
[x]C=[−1−13]
c
[x]C=[−13]
d
[x]C=[3−13]
e
[x]C=[3513]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[1−5], we can write x as follows:

x=b1−5b2=−5b2+b1=−(5b2)−(−b1)=−(5b2)−13(−3b1)=−c1−13c2

Therefore, [x]C=[−1−13].
q-35260.knowledge_point: Writing a Two-Dimensional Vector in a Different Basis

q-34769.name: Question 5
q-34769.problem: Let $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where ${b}_{1}=-{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=3{c}_{1}?$
q-34769.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={c}_{1}-2{c}_{2} \\  & =-2{c}_{2}+{c}_{1} \\  & =2(-{c}_{2})+\frac{1}{3}(3{c}_{1}) \\  & =2{b}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

q-34769.html:
Question 5
?

Let C={c1,c2} be a basis of R2 and [x]C=[1−2]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis B={b1,b2}, where b1=−c2 and b2=3c1?

a
[x]B=[23]
b
[x]B=[−21]
c
[x]B=[−123]
d
[x]B=[132]
e
[x]B=[213]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]C=[1−2], we can write x as follows:

x=c1−2c2=−2c2+c1=2(−c2)+13(3c1)=2b1+13b2

Therefore, [x]B=[213].

q-112652.name: Question 6
q-112652.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-\frac{1}{5}{b}_{3}$, ${c}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}{b}_{1}?$
q-112652.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}-{b}_{3} \\  & =-{b}_{3}+2{b}_{2}+5{b}_{1} \\  & =5(-\frac{1}{5}{b}_{3})+2\cdot 2(\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2})+5\cdot 2(\frac{1}{2}{b}_{1}) \\  & =5{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}+10{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 10\end{aligned}].$

x=5b1+2b2−b3=−b3+2b2+5b1=5(−15b3)+2⋅2(12b2)+5⋅2(12b1)=5c1+4c2+10c3

q-112657.name: Question 7
q-112657.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{b}_{3}$, ${c}_{2}=-\frac{1}{4}{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{3}=2{b}_{1}?$
q-112657.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}+{b}_{3} \\  & ={b}_{3}-2{b}_{2}+4{b}_{1} \\  & =3(\frac{1}{3}{b}_{3})+2\cdot 4(-\frac{1}{4}{b}_{2})+2(2{b}_{1}) \\  & =3{c}_{1}+8{c}_{2}+2{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 8 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[4−21]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=13b3, c2=−14b2 and c3=2b1?

a
[x]C=[34−2]
b
[x]C=[382]
c
[x]C=[248]
d
[x]C=[122]
e
[x]C=[1−31]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[4−21], we can write x as follows:

x=4b1−2b2+b3=b3−2b2+4b1=3(13b3)+2⋅4(−14b2)+2(2b1)=3c1+8c2+2c3

q-112714.name: Question 8
q-112714.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=\frac{3}{4}{b}_{3}$, ${c}_{2}=-\frac{1}{3}{b}_{1}$ and ${c}_{3}=4{b}_{2}?$
q-112714.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}-8{b}_{2}+3{b}_{3} \\  & =3{b}_{3}+2{b}_{1}-8{b}_{2} \\  & =3\cdot \frac{4}{3}(\frac{3}{4}{b}_{3})-2\cdot 3(-\frac{1}{3}{b}_{1})-2(4{b}_{2}) \\  & =4{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2}-2{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

q-112714.html:
Question 8
?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[2−83]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=34b3, c2=−13b1 and c3=4b2?

a
[x]C=[12−2]
b
[x]C=[2−3−2]
c
[x]C=[14−2]
d
[x]C=[4−6−2]
e
[x]C=[63−2]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[2−83], we can write x as follows:

x=2b1−8b2+3b3=3b3+2b1−8b2=3⋅43(34b3)−2⋅3(−13b1)−2(4b2)=4c1−6c2−2c3

Therefore, [x]C=[4−6−2].

q-80815.html:
Question 9
?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[72−1]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=2b3, c2=−3b1 and c3=8b2?

a
[x]C=[−12−7318]
b
[x]C=[−12−7314]
c
[x]C=[234]
d
[x]C=[127314]
e
[x]C=[−2−38]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[72−1], we can write x as follows:

x=7b1+2b2−b3=−b3+7b1+2b2=−12(2b3)−73(−3b1)+14(8b2)=−12c1−73c2+14c3

Therefore, [x]C=[−12−7314].

q-112811.name: Question 10
q-112811.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-3{b}_{2}$, ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{3}$ and ${c}_{3}=3{b}_{1}?$
q-112811.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3{b}_{1}+6{b}_{2}-2{b}_{3} \\  & =6{b}_{2}-2{b}_{3}+3{b}_{1} \\  & =-2(-3{b}_{2})-2{b}_{3}+3{b}_{1} \\  & =-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

q-112811.html:
Question 10
?

Let B={b1,b2,b3} be a basis of R3 and [x]B=[36−2]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2,c3}, where c1=−3b2, c2=2b3 and c3=3b1?

a
[x]C=[1−22]
b
[x]C=[321]
c
[x]C=[2−12]
d
[x]C=[1−21]
e
[x]C=[−2−11]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[36−2], we can write x as follows:

x=3b1+6b2−2b3=6b2−2b3+3b1=−2(−3b2)−2b3+3b1=−2c1−c2+c3

Therefore, [x]C=[−2−11].
q-112811.knowledge_point: Writing a Three-Dimensional Vector in a Different Basis

q-80838.name: Question 11
q-80838.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}-{b}_{2}?$
q-80838.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}-{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Adding the equations, we get 

$$
{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=3{b}_{1}\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=2(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2})+{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}-\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =6{b}_{1}-{b}_{2} \\  & =6(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2})-(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}-\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}-\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{8}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}].$

q-80838.html:
Question 11
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[6−1]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=2b1+b2 and c2=b1−b2?

a
[x]C=[11−7]
b
[x]C=[5383]
c
[x]C=[3−3]
d
[x]C=[4−2]
e
[x]C=[133−53]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=2b1+b2c2=b1−b2.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. Adding the equations, we get

c1+c2=3b1⟹b1=13c1+13c2.

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

c1=2(13c1+13c2)+b2⟹b2=13c1−23c2.

Since [x]B=[6−1], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=6b1−b2=6(13c1+13c2)−(13c1−23c2)=2c1+2c2−13c1+23c2=53c1+83c2

Therefore, [x]C=[5383].

q-80835.name: Question 12
q-80835.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}?$
q-80835.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Multiplying the second equation by $-1$ and adding the equations, we get 

$$
{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}=-{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}={c}_{2}-{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}={b}_{1}+({c}_{2}-{c}_{1})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\  & =2(2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2})+({c}_{2}-{c}_{1}) \\  & =4{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}+{c}_{2}-{c}_{1} \\  & =3{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

q-80835.html:
Question 12
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[21]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=b1+b2 and c2=b1+2b2?

a
[x]C=[5−1]
b
[x]C=[31]
c
[x]C=[5−3]
d
[x]C=[3−1]
e
[x]C=[3−3]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=b1+b2c2=b1+2b2.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. Multiplying the second equation by −1 and adding the equations, we get

c1−c2=−b2⟹b2=c2−c1.

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

c1=b1+(c2−c1)⟹b1=2c1−c2.

Since [x]B=[21], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=2b1+b2=2(2c1−c2)+(c2−c1)=4c1−2c2+c2−c1=3c1−c2

Therefore, [x]C=[3−1].

q-112823.name: Question 13
q-112823.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=3{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-{b}_{2}?$
q-112823.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=3{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the second equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=-{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=3{b}_{1}-2(-{c}_{2})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=\frac{{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}}{3}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =9{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2} \\  & =9(\frac{{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}}{3})+2(-{c}_{2}) \\  & =3{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2}-2{c}_{2} \\  & =3{c}_{1}-8{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8\end{aligned}].$

q-112823.html:
Question 13
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[92]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=3b1−2b2 and c2=−b2?

a
[x]C=[16]
b
[x]C=[−5−6]
c
[x]C=[2−4]
d
[x]C=[3−8]
e
[x]C=[−3−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=3b1−2b2c2=−b2.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. From the second equation, we get

b2=−c2.

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

c1=3b1−2(−c2)⟹b1=c1−2c23.

Since [x]B=[92], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=9b1+2b2=9(c1−2c23)+2(−c2)=3c1−6c2−2c2=3c1−8c2

Therefore, [x]C=[3−8].

q-80635.name: Question 14
q-80635.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}={b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}?$
q-80635.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}={b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Multiplying the second equation by $2$ and adding the equations, we get 

$$
{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}=3{b}_{1}\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2})-2{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}=-\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2} \\  & =2(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{2}{3}{c}_{2})-3(-\frac{1}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{4}{3}{c}_{2}+{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

q-80635.html:
Question 14
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[2−3]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=b1−2b2 and c2=b1+b2?

a
[x]C=[−53−23]
b
[x]C=[13−23]
c
[x]C=[53−43]
d
[x]C=[5313]
e
[x]C=[−2353]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=b1−2b2c2=b1+b2.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. Multiplying the second equation by 2 and adding the equations, we get

c1+2c2=3b1⟹b1=13c1+23c2.

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

c1=(13c1+23c2)−2b2⟹b2=−13c1+13c2.

Since [x]B=[2−3], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=2b1−3b2=2(13c1+23c2)−3(−13c1+13c2)=23c1+43c2+c1−c2=53c1+13c2

Therefore, [x]C=[5313].

q-80830.name: Question 15
q-80830.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1}?$
q-80830.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=-{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the first equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=-{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{2}=-{c}_{1}-{b}_{1}\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=-{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3{b}_{1}+5{b}_{2} \\  & =3(-{c}_{1}-{c}_{2})+5(-{c}_{1}) \\  & =-3{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}-5{c}_{1} \\  & =-8{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$

q-80830.html:
Question 15
?

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[35]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=−b2 and c2=b2−b1?

a
[x]C=[−8−3]
b
[x]C=[7−3]
c
[x]C=[−33]
d
[x]C=[23]
e
[x]C=[−7−3]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=−b2c2=b2−b1.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. From the first equation, we get

b2=−c1.

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

c2=−c1−b1⟹b1=−c1−c2.

Since [x]B=[35], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=3b1+5b2=3(−c1−c2)+5(−c1)=−3c1−3c2−5c1=−8c1−3c2

Therefore, [x]C=[−8−3]
